name: mta-p2-user
title: Malware traffic analysis, Part 2: who is the user

slides.title: The alerts gave me an IP address. The ticket needed a person.
slides.sub: Host name, MAC, user and full name from one exercise pcap, each checked in a second protocol where I could.

slides.title: DHCP gave the host name and MAC.
body: Frame 1830, DHCP Request: option 12 host name, option 50 requested IP, option 61 MAC.
slides.caption: DESKTOP-5NLV63K asked for 172.16.8[.]49 at 02:08:12 UTC.

slides.title: Kerberos named the user.
body: Computer accounts end in $, so I filtered them out.
slides.caption: Frame 2816: AS-REP for rvance in FIRSTTOLAST.TECH.

slides.title: Kerberos also confirmed the host name.
slides.caption: Frame 2698: TGS-REP for the computer account DESKTOP-5NLV63K$.

slides.title: SAMR gave the full name.
slides.caption: Frame 2947: account rvance, full name Raymond Vance.

slides.title: Each fact, checked twice where I could
bullets: MAC: DHCP option 61 and the Ethernet header (2816)
Full name: SAMR only. One source, and I wrote that down.

slides.title: Cheat sheet: who is behind an IP
bullets: Host, IP, MAC: `dhcp.option.hostname == "<host>"`, then read options 12, 50 and 61
Check each fact in a second protocol. Note the ones you can't.

body: 131 requests to 15 domains, and the pattern that tied them together.
